title: MRI radiomics supports individualized Duchenne disease-trajectory reconstruction
summary: XGBoost combined baseline MRI radiomics and clinical features to estimate muscle fat-fraction trajectory parameters in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The final dataset included 98 unique participants, with 68 soleus and 64 vastus-lateralis analyses; held-out reconstructed trajectories had reported mean absolute errors of 0.04 and 0.06. Targets came from a previously fitted nonlinear mixed-effects model, rather than directly observed trajectory parameters. The retrospective analysis identified candidate progression subgroups but did not establish treatment response, prospective prediction or external generalizability.

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: Held-out participant trajectory reconstruction compared with observed longitudinal fat fractions.
evidence.unknown: Independent cohort validation, robustness of derived targets and benefits for clinical trial design remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Participant-level 80:20 train/test split; XGBoost estimates NLME-derived trajectory descriptors from baseline radiomic/clinical features; reconstruction compared with observed fat fraction. Derived targets can shrink sparse subject trajectories; this is not new prospective clinical utility.
